title: Chapter 103 — Operations Literacy: Why Every Salesperson Needs It
intro: The operational knowledge that separates the professional from the order-taker.

sections.title: Operations Is Sales Infrastructure
sections.content:
Most salespeople think their job starts at the greeting and ends at the close. The professional knows that operations — inventory, delivery, purchasing, returns, and store economics — is the foundation everything else sits on.

When you promise delivery next Thursday, you are making an operational commitment. When you quote a price, you are working within a margin structure. When you sell a package with installation, you are triggering a logistics chain. If you do not understand these systems, you will make promises you cannot keep — and broken promises are the most expensive mistake in retail.

Operational literacy does not mean you need to run the warehouse. It means you need to understand inventory statuses before you promise availability. You need to understand delivery scheduling before you commit a date. You need to understand margin structure before you discount.

sections.title: The Salesperson's Operations Checklist
sections.content:
Before every sale, verify: is the product in stock and available — not just on-hand, but actually sellable? Can we deliver on the date I am about to promise? Are the installation requirements met — gas line, electrical, water supply, path clearance? Is the haul-away included or extra? Are there any pending price changes, promotions ending, or model discontinuations?

This checklist takes 60 seconds. It prevents the most common complaints in appliance retail: wrong delivery date, out-of-stock surprises, and installation failures.

sections.title: Speaking Operations
sections.content:
Learn the language. On-hand versus available versus committed. Lead time versus delivery window. Gross margin versus net margin. Inventory turns. COGS. Restocking fees.

When you speak operations fluently, your manager trusts you more, your delivery team respects you more, and your customers experience fewer problems. Operational literacy is a career accelerator that nobody teaches in sales training — until now.
